title: Senior Engineer / Lead - Battery Management Systems
jobDescription: Job Summary : Joining Ultraviolette as an Electronics Engineer specializing in Battery Management Systems (BMS), you will have a vital role in the creation and advancement of state-of-the-art, high-performance electric vehicle technology with a global reach. Strong understanding of battery characteristics, chemistry, charging algorithms, and safety considerations. Experience with battery cell balancing techniques and algorithms. Knowledge of relevant industry standards and regulations related to battery technology and electric vehicles. Familiarity with embedded systems and firmware development for BMS applications. Ability to analyze and interpret battery performance data using relevant software tools. Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail. Job Summary : 

Joining Ultraviolette as an Electronics Engineer specializing in Battery Management Systems (BMS), you will have a vital role in the creation and advancement of state-of-the-art, high-performance electric vehicle technology with a global reach. Your main responsibility will center around designing, implementing, and optimizing the BMS for the electric motorcycle's battery pack, ensuring seamless operation and optimal performance. 

Job Responsibities :  
​

  1. Design and develop Battery Management Systems (BMS) for electric motorcycle battery packs, ensuring efficient and reliable operation. 

  1. Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including mechanical engineers, firmware engineers, and system architects, to integrate BMS seamlessly into the overall electric vehicle system. 

  1. Perform detailed circuit design, schematic capture, and PCB layout for BMS modules and associated electronics. 

  1. Conduct testing and validation of BMS prototypes to ensure compliance with safety standards, performance requirements, and regulatory guidelines. 

  1. Analyze battery performance data, including voltage, current, temperature, and state of charge, to optimize BMS algorithms and enhance battery efficiency and lifespan. 

  1. Collaborate with cell suppliers to define battery specifications, conduct cell characterization, and validation. 

  1. Troubleshoot and debug BMS-related issues during development, production, and field operation phases. 

  1. Stay up to date with the latest advancements in BMS technology, battery chemistries, and industry trends, and integrate them into the design process. 



Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree or higher in Electronics Engineering or Electrical Engineering.
  • Proven experience in the design and development of Battery Management Systems (BMS) for lithium-ion battery packs. 
  • In-depth knowledge of Circuit Design, Analysis and Simulation 
  • Proficiency in Simulation, schematic capture, and PCB layout tools. 
  • Strong understanding of battery characteristics, chemistry, charging algorithms, and safety considerations. 
  • Experience with battery cell balancing techniques and algorithms. 
  • Knowledge of relevant industry standards and regulations related to battery technology and electric vehicles. 
  • Familiarity with embedded systems and firmware development for BMS applications. 
  • Ability to analyze and interpret battery performance data using relevant software tools. 
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail. 
  • Effective communication and collaboration skills to work in a cross-functional team environment.
  • Strong understanding of electrical and electrochemical principles related to battery systems. 
  • Proficiency in battery simulation and analysis tools, such as MATLAB or equivalent 
  • Experience with PCB design tools, such as OrCAD, Cadence, or equivalent 
  • Proficient in programming languages, such as C, C++, or Python, for embedded systems and data analysis 
  • Familiarity with design for manufacturing (DFM) and design for assembly (DFA) principles for electronics and battery systems 
  • Knowledge of safety and failure analysis techniques for battery systems, such as fault tree analysis (FTA) and failure modes and effects analysis (FMEA)

title: Assistant Manager - Supplier Qualiity (Forging, Machining & Die Casting)
jobDescription: Supplier Quality - Asst Manager will drive exceptional product quality and continuous improvement across the external supplier base for mechanical commodities. Serving as the internal and external Subject Matter Expert will lead supplier onboarding, ensure First Time Right parts for New Product Introductions and oversee robust Process & System audits. Key Responsibilities 1.Commodity Expertise & Technical Leadership · Act as the technical expert for casting (High Pressure, Low Pressure, Gravity Die Casting), open/closed die forging, and complex CNC machining processes. · Collaborate with Engineering on Design for Manufacturing (DFM) and Design/Process FMEA exercises to proactively mitigate manufacturing risks. · Review part design, dimensional tolerances, and geometric dimensioning & tolerancing (GD&T) to ensure manufacturability and compliance with global standards. · Process Standardization: Define quality parameters, review engineering drawings, and establish clear measurement/inspection standards for machined and fabricated parts 2. Supplier Evaluation & Development · Supplier selection, capability assessments, and facility audits for new and existing suppliers. · Execute and monitor the Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP) framework and Production Part Approval Process (PPAP) for all new / existing parts. · Develop and execute performance improvement plans for underperforming suppliers through training in Lean and Six Sigma methodologies. 3 . Quality Control & Issue Resolution · Manage the Non-Conformance Material Report (NCMR) process and lead root cause analysis (RCA) and Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) implementations at supplier sites. · Establish measurement system analysis (MSA) and ensure testing protocols (CMM, Heat treatment process , Non-destructive test (NDT) , Die penetration test , Magnetic Particle Inspection (MPI), Ultrasonic Testing (UT), Micro-hardness testing, Grain size analysis · Conduct on-site verification of corrective actions during critical quality failures 4. Operational & Supplier Governance • Daily Performance Monitoring: Track supplier Parts Per Million (PPM), Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ), and On-Time Delivery (OTD) for the designated commodity portfolio. • Supplier Risk Management: Maintain a dynamic "Supplier Risk Matrix" categorizing vendors by financial health, capacity constraints, tooling life, and quality history. • Escalation Management: Serve as the final point of escalation for chronic supplier quality issues, issuing formal Supplier Quality Alerts and placing vendors on "Quality Hold" or "Controlled Shipping" when necessary. 5. Deep-Dive Process Control (Commodity-Specific) • Die Casting: Validate thermal management systems, shot-sleeve parameters, molten metal degassing practices, die-coat applications, and porosity controls (X-ray/CT scan reviews). • Forging: Oversee billet heating temperature profiles, grain flow orientation verification, die wear tracking, and post-forge heat treatment lines (Annealing, Quetching & Tempering). • Machining: Review CNC fixture repeatability, tool wear compensation protocols, coolant concentration management, and coordinate measuring machine (CMM) programming alignments. • Metallurgy: Strong understanding of microstructural analysis, defect identification (e.g., shrinkage porosity, cold shuts, forging laps, decarburization). 6. Painting & Surface Finishing (Liquid & Powder Coating) Chemical Pre-treatment: Audit the supplier’s multi-stage pre-treatment line Electrodeposition (CED/E-Coat) Powder & Liquid Application Coating Testing & Validation Requirements Qualifications & Competencies • Education: Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, Metallurgy, or Production Engineering. • Experience: 8–12+ years of progressive experience in supplier quality or vendor development functions within manufacturing or automotive industries • Technical Skills: Deep metallurgical understanding, GD&T mastery, capability in interpreting industry standards (ASTM, ISO 9001, IATF 16949).

Supplier Quality - Asst Manager will drive exceptional product quality and continuous improvement across the external supplier base for mechanical commodities. Serving as the internal and external Subject Matter Expert will lead supplier onboarding, ensure First Time Right parts for New Product Introductions and oversee robust Process & System audits.

Key Responsibilities

1.Commodity Expertise & Technical Leadership

·       Act as the technical expert for casting (High Pressure, Low Pressure, Gravity Die Casting), open/closed die forging, and complex CNC machining processes.

·       Collaborate with Engineering on Design for Manufacturing (DFM) and Design/Process FMEA exercises to proactively mitigate manufacturing risks.

·       Review part design, dimensional tolerances, and geometric dimensioning & tolerancing (GD&T) to ensure manufacturability and compliance with global standards.

·       Process Standardization: Define quality parameters, review engineering drawings, and establish clear measurement/inspection standards for machined and fabricated parts

2. Supplier Evaluation & Development

·       Supplier selection, capability assessments, and facility audits for new and existing suppliers.

·       Execute and monitor the Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP) framework and Production Part Approval Process (PPAP) for all new / existing parts.

·       Develop and execute performance improvement plans for underperforming suppliers through training in Lean and Six Sigma methodologies.

3. Quality Control & Issue Resolution

·       Manage the Non-Conformance Material Report (NCMR) process and lead root cause analysis (RCA) and Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) implementations at supplier sites.

·       Establish measurement system analysis (MSA) and ensure testing protocols (CMM, Heat treatment process , Non-destructive test (NDT) , Die penetration test  , Magnetic Particle Inspection (MPI), Ultrasonic Testing (UT), Micro-hardness testing, Grain size analysis

·       Conduct on-site verification of corrective actions during critical quality failures

4. Operational & Supplier Governance

•       Daily Performance Monitoring: Track supplier Parts Per Million (PPM), Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ), and On-Time Delivery (OTD) for the designated commodity portfolio.

•       Supplier Risk Management: Maintain a dynamic "Supplier Risk Matrix" categorizing vendors by financial health, capacity constraints, tooling life, and quality history.

•       Escalation Management: Serve as the final point of escalation for chronic supplier quality issues, issuing formal Supplier Quality Alerts and placing vendors on "Quality Hold" or "Controlled Shipping" when necessary.

5. Deep-Dive Process Control (Commodity-Specific)

•       Die Casting: Validate thermal management systems, shot-sleeve parameters, molten metal degassing practices, die-coat applications, and porosity controls (X-ray/CT scan reviews).

•       Forging: Oversee billet heating temperature profiles, grain flow orientation verification, die wear tracking, and post-forge heat treatment lines (Annealing, Quetching & Tempering).

•       Machining: Review CNC fixture repeatability, tool wear compensation protocols, coolant concentration management, and coordinate measuring machine (CMM) programming alignments.

•       Metallurgy: Strong understanding of microstructural analysis, defect identification (e.g., shrinkage porosity, cold shuts, forging laps, decarburization).

6. Painting & Surface Finishing (Liquid & Powder Coating)

  • Chemical Pre-treatment: Audit the supplier’s multi-stage pre-treatment line
  • Electrodeposition (CED/E-Coat)
  • Powder & Liquid Application
  • Coating Testing & Validation


Requirements

Qualifications & Competencies

•       Education: Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, Metallurgy, or Production Engineering.

•       Experience: 8–12+ years of progressive experience in supplier quality or vendor development functions within manufacturing or automotive industries

•       Technical Skills: Deep metallurgical understanding, GD&T mastery, capability in interpreting industry standards (ASTM, ISO 9001, IATF 16949).

title: Principal Electronics Engineer - Embedded Hardware
jobDescription: Join the Charge. Create the Future. At Ultraviolette, we're more than a company—we’re a movement. A movement that's pushing the boundaries of what's possible in electric mobility. From engineering India’s Fastest Motorcycle to designing The World’s Most Advanced Electric Scooter, we thrive on innovation, audacity, and the relentless pursuit of performance. We’re a diverse team of trailblazers, engineers, designers, creatives and visionaries—united by a shared obsession: to craft machines that are not only sustainable but exhilarating. Here, radical design meets intelligent technology, and every line of code or bolt of hardware brings us closer to reshaping the future of mobility. Our mission is to accelerate the evolution of mobility across the globe - and we’re just getting started. If you're driven by purpose, inspired by possibility, and ready to build something that truly matters, Ultraviolette is the place where your ambition becomes impact. Let's create the future—together. As a Principal/Lead Electronics Engineer – Embedded Hardware , your roles and responsibilities include: 1. Vehicle Electronics Architecture Design, build and bring into production high performance electronics hardware such as vehicle control units, display clusters, telematics that include RF circuits, and sensor electronics. Extract requirements from different component systems, firmware systems, software systems and vehicle systems to define architectures for high-speed electronic design of control units and telematics. Develop and maintain system-level schematics, interface definitions, and communication protocols (CAN, LIN, UART, SPI, I2C). 2. Embedded Systems Design Design the architecture and native hardware using high-speed, high-performance microprocessors and micro-controllers for supporting automotive OS, graphics, vision systems, audio systems, radar/LIDAR systems. Architect and design/validate connected vehicle systems including GNSS, LTE, BLE and Wi-Fi. Lead the design, development and integration of embedded hardware for vehicle functions such as lighting, indicators, horn, immobiliser, cluster and IMUs. Collaborate with firmware teams to define hardware-software interfaces, bootloaders, and OTA update mechanisms. 3. Diagnostics & Compliance Develop and implement UDS-based diagnostics, fault logging, and service tools. Ensure compliance with AIS-004, ISO 26262, and other relevant automotive manufacturing and design standards. 4. Testing & Validation Define and execute test plans for bench-level and vehicle-level validation. Use tools like Vector CANoe , CANalyzer, ETAS INCA, oscilloscopes, network/spectrum analysers for debugging and validation. 5. Cross-functional Collaboration Work closely with mechanical, software, powertrain, wire-harness, and UX teams to ensure system-level integration. Work with cloud and mobile app teams to ensure real-time data streaming, diagnostics, and remote-control features. Participate in design reviews, FMEA sessions, and field issue resolution. Requirements What we are looking for: B.E./B. Tech or M.E./M. Debugging support: capture CAN/diagnostic logs and test notes, perform approved electrical or interface checks under supervision, support structured issue isolation, and assist with regression and fix verification. Systems thinking, curiosity, enthusiasm and the ability to follow one function across multiple controllers and interfaces. Basic understanding of embedded systems, CAN, sensors, actuators, state machines, diagnostics and fault logic. title: Design Engineer - Plastics
jobDescription: Job Summary We are seeking a detail-oriented Plastic Design Engineer to join our 2-Wheeler Electric Vehicle R&D team. You will design, develop, and optimize plastic components like body panels, trims, and battery enclosures. Your role focuses on balancing structural integrity, weight reduction, aesthetics, and manufacturing feasibility. Key Responsibilities Product Design: Create 3D models and 2D engineering drawings for 2W plastic components. DFM/DFA: Apply Design for Manufacturing and Assembly principles for injection moulding. Material Selection: Choose appropriate engineering plastics based on thermal, mechanical, and UV requirements. CAE Collaboration: Work with CAE/VI/Proto teams to review DFS , FEA, and vibration analysis results. Supplier Alignment: Coordinate with toolmakers to review Mold designs and resolve tooling issues. Testing & Validation: Define testing criteria and support physical validation of plastic parts. Design and Development : Collaborate with cross-functional teams to develop innovative mechanical designs for new products or improve existing ones. Use NX / teamcenter software tools to create detailed 2D and 3D models, assembly drawings, DFM, DFMEA, DFA, DFS and technical specifications. Upfront involvement with supplier for part manufacturing and quality achievement. Perform GDNT and layout integration for mechanical electronics design and development. Conceptualization : Generate concepts and perform feasibility studies to evaluate the viability of new product ideas or design modifications for Proprietary design. Conduct research and analysis to identify the best materials (Polymers), components, and manufacturing processes to achieve desired performance, cost, regulatory and quality targets. Engineering Analysis : Support engineering calculations, simulations, and finite element analysis (FEA) to assess mechanical system performance, structural integrity, and thermal characteristics. Identify and resolve design issues, ensuring compliance with industry standards and regulations. Prototyping and Testing : Create prototypes or coordinate with prototype manufacturing teams to build physical models for evaluation and testing. Conduct tests and measurements to verify design performance, identify areas for improvement, and make necessary design iterations. Documentation and Reporting : Prepare comprehensive engineering documentation, including design specifications, bills of materials (BOMs), assembly instructions, and technical reports. Maintain accurate records of design changes, test results, and project milestones. Collaboration and Communication : Work closely with multidisciplinary teams, including electrical engineers, manufacturing engineers, and project managers, to ensure effective integration of mechanical designs into larger systems. Communicate design concepts, ideas, and technical information clearly and effectively to stakeholders. Continuous Improvement : Stay updated and benchmark with the latest industry trends, technologies, and best practices related to mechanical design. Seek opportunities to enhance design processes, tools, and methodologies to drive efficiency, productivity, and innovation Requirements Education: Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, Automotive, or Plastics Engineering. Experience: 2 to 4 years of core plastic product design experience, preferably in automotive or 2W OEMs. CAD Software: Advanced proficiency in Siemens NX & Teamcenter . Tooling Insight: Basic knowledge of injection Mold construction, lifters, sliders, and gate locations. GD&T: Practical experience applying Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing per ASME standards.

About the Role:

The Vehicle Dynamics Components (VDC) engineering team is responsible for the design, development, and integration of systems that ensure superior ride quality, handling, and safety for our next-generation electric motorcycle/Scooter platforms.

As a Senior Engineer for Suspension Systems, you will move beyond simple catalogue selection. You will lead the integration, technical evaluation, and geometric packaging of suspension system components. This role balances rigorous first-principles engineering with end-to-end ownership of vendor coordination, physical testing, and manufacturing quality.


· CAD Modelling & Drafting (NX & Teamcenter): Create production-ready 3D models and detailed 2D engineering drawings for front forks, rear shock absorbers, triple clamps (upper/lower), and handlebar raisers in Siemens NX.

· Component Sizing & Integration: Own the mathematical sizing selection, and packaging of the front forks and rear shock absorbers, establishing optimal damping rates, spring characteristics, and travel constraints.

· Structural Design & DFx: Design high-strength chassis interfaces like triple clamps etc. utilizing aluminium high-pressure die casting (HPDC), AL/Steel forgings, and precision machining while applying strict DFM/DFA principles.

· Technical Specifications: Author comprehensive technical requirements, performance targets, and engineering specifications for the entire suspension, steering and handlebar module.

· Concept & Option Evaluation: Lead concept generation and trade-off studies for front fork geometries (offset, trail) and rear shock layouts based on supplier inputs and vehicle dynamic constraints (anti-squat, anti-dive etc.).

· Cross-Functional SPOC: Act as the Single Point of Contact (SPOC) to coordinate technical delivery and packaging boundaries between internal engineering teams and external Tier-1 suppliers.

· DVP & Test Planning: Develop and execute comprehensive Design Verification Plans (DVP) and structural test setups to validate the forks, shocks, and clamps against extreme real-world load cases.

· Quality Frameworks: Implement design FMEAs (DFMEA) and adhere to a structured Design Maturity Model to systematically de-risk component design & development.

· Root Cause Analysis: Troubleshoot and resolve complex assembly line and field failures (e.g., fluid leaks, fork binding, handle vibrations) using structured methods like Pareto charts, Ishikawa, and 5-Why analysis.

Experience & Qualifications

· Education & Experience: B.Tech/ B.E in Mechanical Engg. with 3 to 7 years of dedicated experience in suspension, steering assembly, and chassis component design.

· Technical Competency: Expert-level proficiency in Siemens NX and Teamcenter PLM, with a deep first-principles understanding of front-end motorcycle geometry, structural casting/forging design, and homologation standards.

· Supplier Management: Proven track record of managing technical partnerships with Tier-1 suspension and proprietary component manufacturers from initial concept to final production release.

Nice-to-Have Competencies

· Vehicle Testing: Practical hands-on experience in suspension tuning.

· Quality Frameworks: Familiarity with Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP), PPAP processes, and Six Sigma problem-solving methodologies for structural casting and forging defects.

· Advanced Kinematics & FEA: Experience using FEA tools (Ansys/Nastran) for stress/fatigue modelling of triple clamps, or Multi-Body Dynamics (MBD) to simulate suspension kinematics.

2. Product Scope

  • Android-based Instrument Cluster (AOSP / Android Automotive)
  • Cluster UI, animations, alerts, and critical ride screens
  • Android system services and background processes
  • Vehicle signal integration (CAN, ECUs)
  • OTA updates (A/B updates, rollback, recovery)

3. Key Responsibilities

3.1 Automation Strategy & Ownership

  • Define and own the end-to-end automation strategy for the Android cluster
  • Decide what must be automated vs manual based on safety, risk, and stability
  • Define automation coverage targets and release gating criteria
  • Ensure automation is designed for embedded hardware, not emulators alone

3.2 Automation Framework Development

  • Design and maintain automation frameworks for:
    • Cluster UI screens, alerts, and transitions
    • Android system services and background components
    • Boot, suspend, resume, and reboot scenarios
  • Enable hardware‑in‑the‑loop (HIL) based automation for realistic testing

3.3 Android System & Stability Testing

  • Automate validation of:
    • Cold boot and warm boot performance
    • ANRs, crashes, watchdog resets
    • Memory leaks, CPU/GPU load, and thermal limits
  • Measure and track application launch time (cold / warm start)
  • Validate touch response latency and input-to-render timing
  • Work closely with Android developers to improve testability and observability

3.4 Power, Performance & Connectivity Metrics

  • Define and automate power measurement and tracking for the cluster
  • Measure current consumption across key states:
    • Boot, idle, ride, standby, sleep
  • Track performance KPIs:
    • Touch response latency
    • UI frame rate and jank
    • App launch time
  • Automate validation of connectivity performance:
    • Bluetooth pairing, reconnect, latency, and stability
    • Wi-Fi scan, connect, throughput, and recovery
    • Network loss and recovery scenarios

3.5 Vehicle Signal & State Validation

  • Automate cluster behavior against:
    • CAN signals and ECU inputs
    • Vehicle state transitions (ride, park, charge, fault)
    • Fault injection and degraded‑mode scenarios
  • Ensure deterministic and safe behavior for safety‑critical displays

3.6 OTA & Release Validation

  • Automate OTA validation for:
    • A/B updates and slot switching
    • Interrupted updates (power or network loss)
    • Rollback and recovery scenarios
  • Validate post‑OTA stability, data integrity, and performance

3.7 Service & Field Issue Support

  • Convert field and service issues into regression automation tests
  • Enable reproducible failure validation on benches
  • Support root‑cause analysis using logs, traces, and automation data

3.8 CI/CD & Reporting

  • Integrate automation into CI pipelines (Jenkins / GitLab CI)
  • Enable unattended test execution on hardware benches
  • Publish clear, actionable reports for engineering and leadership
  • Track regressions and prevent recurrence

4. Test Tools & Automation Stack

Android UI & App Automation

  • UI Automator – Primary framework for system‑level UI and cluster screens
  • Espresso – App‑level automation for system applications
  • Monkey / MonkeyRunner – Input stress and endurance testing

Android System & Compliance

  • CTS (Compatibility Test Suite)
  • VTS (Vendor Test Suite)
  • GTS (Google Test Suite)
  • Android Test Station (ATS) for orchestrating CTS/VTS on hardware

Performance & Stability

  • Perfetto / Systrace – System tracing and latency analysis
  • Simpleperf – CPU profiling
  • dumpsys (gfxinfo, meminfo, activity, power)
  • logcat, tombstones, ANR traces

Stress, Reliability & Power Testing

  • Monkey (long‑run execution)
  • stress‑ng (where supported)
  • Automated reboot, suspend–resume, and power‑cycle loops

OTA & Update Validation

  • A/B OTA testing tools
  • adb sideload and OTA simulation scripts
  • update_engine logs, rollback and recovery validation

Connectivity & Network Testing

  • adb network tools
  • tc (traffic control) for latency and packet loss
  • iptables for network drop scenarios
  • Modem AT‑command tools

CI & Orchestration

  • Jenkins / GitLab CI
  • Custom Python‑based test runners
  • Automated reporting (Allure / HTML dashboards)

5. Skills & Experience

  • 7–12+ years in test automation for Android or embedded systems
  • Strong experience testing Android AOSP / Android Automotive at system level
  • Excellent coding skills in Python (mandatory)
  • Working knowledge of Java / Kotlin for Android integration
  • Understanding of vehicle signals, CAN, diagnostics, and ECU behavior
  • Strong debugging skills using logs, traces, and performance tools
  • Excellent coding skills in Python (mandatory) for automation frameworks, HIL control, and CI integration
  • Hands-on experience with:  UI Automator (mandatory) for system-level UI testing , Espresso for system/app-level validation , Monkey / MonkeyRunner for stress and endurance testing
  • working Knowledge of YOCTO is huge plus

Company: Ultraviolette Automotive


1. Role Overview

Ultraviolette Automotive is building a deeply connected, software‑defined electric motorcycle platform. The Product Manager – Connected Vehicle & Digital Platforms will own the end‑to‑end product lifecycle of the instrument cluster, vehicle‑to‑cloud (IoT) backend, mobile application, and internal dashboards, ensuring a cohesive, reliable, and scalable user experience across riders, service teams, factory operations, and business stakeholders.

This role bridges hardware, embedded software, cloud, mobile apps, UX, service operations, and GTM, translating real‑world EV use cases into crisp product requirements and executable roadmaps.


2. Product Scope

  • Digital Instrument Cluster (Android / Linux based)
  • Vehicle Telemetry & IoT Platform (Cloud ingestion, APIs, analytics)
  • Mobile App (Rider app)
  • Web Dashboards (Service, Factory, Ops, Management)
  • OTA Updates (Cluster, ECUs, firmware, configs)
  • Diagnostics, Logs, Remote Commands

3. Responsibilities by Product Lifecycle Phase


3.1 Product Discovery & Vision

  • Define product vision for Ultraviolette’s connected vehicle ecosystem aligned with brand positioning (performance‑driven, aviation‑inspired, premium EV).
  • Identify rider, service, factory, and business pain points through field data, service feedback, and ride analytics.
  • Convert IoT telemetry possibilities into meaningful rider features (range confidence, performance insights, safety alerts).
  • Own long‑term roadmap for cluster, app, and backend platforms.

3.2 Requirements & User Stories

  • Create clear, testable user stories with acceptance criteria for:
    • Cluster UI/UX flows
    • App‑to‑vehicle interactions
    • Vehicle‑to‑cloud data pipelines
    • Server‑side dashboards
  • Explicitly capture edge cases:
    • Network loss / intermittent connectivity
    • Partial OTA failures
    • Vehicle power cycles mid‑operation
    • Region‑specific regulations (India / EU)
  • Maintain Product Requirement Documents (PRDs) and epics across multiple teams.
  • Act as a single source of truth for product behavior.

3.3 UX & Experience Ownership

  • Own end‑to‑end UX consistency across:
    • Instrument cluster
    • Mobile app
    • Web dashboards
  • Define UX principles for riding scenarios (glanceability, safety, latency sensitivity).
  • Work with design teams to validate flows using real riding and service scenarios.
  • Ensure cluster and app behavior remains intuitive under degraded conditions.

3.4 IoT & Backend Product Ownership

  • Define telemetry schemas (what data, frequency, priority).
  • Own API contracts between vehicle, cloud, and apps.
  • Prioritize scalability, security, and data integrity.
  • Define analytics requirements for:
    • Rider behavior
    • Vehicle health
    • Warranty and failure prediction

3.5 OTA & Software Lifecycle Management

  • Own OTA strategy across cluster and ECUs:
    • Full vs delta updates
    • Rollback and recovery strategies
    • Region‑specific releases
  • Define release trains and update eligibility rules.
  • Coordinate staged roll outs and monitor post‑OTA health metrics.
  • Ensure OTA flows align with service and also comply with homologation constraints.

3.6 Factory & Manufacturing Collaboration

  • Define factory software workflows:
    • Vehicle provisioning
    • VIN binding
    • Software flashing and validation
  • Ensure traceability of software versions to vehicle batches.
  • Support factory dashboards for diagnostics and audit readiness.
  • Collaborate with manufacturing teams to minimize line disruptions due to software.

3.7 Service & After‑Sales Collaboration

  • Partner with service teams to define:
    • Remote diagnostics
    • Error code interpretation
    • Log access and tooling
  • Translate service pain points into backlog items.
  • Enable predictive maintenance use cases using telemetry.
  • Support dealer and service SOPs with digital tools.

3.8 Go‑To‑Market (GTM) & Launch Readiness

  • Own feature readiness for vehicle launches and software drops.
  • Coordinate with marketing on feature narratives and rider communication.
  • Ensure app, backend, and cluster features are launch‑ready and region‑compliant.
  • Support launch metrics tracking and post‑launch issue triage.

3.9 Metrics & Continuous Improvement

  • Define KPIs for connected products:
    • OTA success rate
    • App engagement
    • Cluster stability metrics
    • Telemetry coverage
  • Use data to refine roadmap and backlog prioritization.
  • Drive continuous improvement culture across digital platforms.

4. Stakeholder Management

  • Engineering: Embedded, Android/Linux, Cloud, Mobile
  • Design & UX
  • Service & After‑Sales
  • Factory & Operations
  • Quality & Homologation
  • Marketing & GTM
  • Leadership team

5. Skills & Experience

  • 6–10+ years in product management for embedded, IoT, or automotive systems.
  • Strong understanding of:
    • Connected vehicles / IoT architectures
    • OTA systems
    • Embedded software constraints
  • Proven ability to write crisp user stories and PRDs.
  • Experience working with cross‑functional hardware and software teams.
  • Data‑driven mindset with strong analytical skills.

6. Mindset & Cultural Fit

  • Systems thinker who understands vehicle + cloud + user holistically.
  • Comfortable dealing with ambiguity and complex edge cases.
  • Strong ownership mentality—bias for clarity and execution.
  • Passion for EVs, performance engineering, and rider experience.

title: Industralization Engineer
jobDescription: Role Summary: We are looking for a hands-on and technically sound Electronics Industrialization Engineer to drive the transition of products from design to scalable, high-quality manufacturing. This role is a critical interface between R&D, sourcing, and EMS partners , ensuring design intent is preserved while enabling cost-effective, reliable mass production. The ideal candidate should have a strong foundation in power electronics , a working understanding of embedded software , and practical experience in EMS collaboration and DFM . As an Industrialization Engineer at Ultraviolette Automotive, your roles and responsibilities will be to: Technical Ownership & Industrialization: Lead the industrialization lifecycle from prototype (EVT) through validation (DVT/PVT) to mass production. Translate engineering design into production-ready documentation (BOMs, gerbers, PCBA specs, test jigs). Perform design for manufacturability (DFM) and design for testability (DFT) reviews. Own ramp-up quality metrics such as yield, test coverage, and field return trends . Work with R&D on thermal design reviews , layout strategies , and power component derating . Ensure compliance with voltage isolation , creepage/clearance , and safety standards. Act as the technical bridge between internal R&D, sourcing/procurement, and EMS partners. Evaluate and qualify suppliers and alternate components , driving cost engineering without compromising quality. Coordinate with EMS on NPI builds , line setup, process validation, and first article inspection (FAI) . Assist in issue resolution across mechanical fit, electrical issues, firmware compatibility, and yield drops. Support flashing, validation, and version control of firmware at the EMS line. Work closely with software teams to validate hardware-software integration under production conditions. Requirements Qualifications & Skills: B.E./B.Tech in Electronics, Electrical, or related discipline. 5–10 years of experience in hardware industrialization Solid knowledge of PCB design reviews , SMT/PCBA manufacturing, and box build. Working knowledge of Altium, OrCAD , or similar for PCB-level discussions. Experience with test development , ICT/FCT setups, fixture design and test station qualification . Comfortable reviewing or discussing schematics, layouts, and thermal design . Familiar with component lifecycle management , cost down strategies , and BOM optimization . Familiarity with firmware flashing tools , basic embedded debug (e.g., serial logs, GPIO), and validation steps. Hands-on experience interacting with EMS vendors and component suppliers . Strong communication skills to manage cross-functional coordination . Willingness to travel to EMS and supplier sites as needed. Experience in cost down and value engineering . Preferred (Nice to Have): Working knowledge of FMEA, APQP, PPAP, or ISO/IATF processes . Familiarity with compliance and safety standards (e.g., IEC, ISO26262 for functional safety).

  • Create 3D models and engineering drawings for new products using CAD software (NX)

  • Analyze and resolve design and manufacturing issues, implementing improvements to increase efficiency and productivity, and ensure compliance with quality and safety standards
  • Work closely with suppliers to ensure component quality and delivery, leveraging supplier partnerships and collaborative development processes.
  • Provide technical leadership and guidance to junior engineers and designers, mentoring and training as needed


Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering or related field
  • 5-7 years of experience in mechanical engineering, with a focus on product development and design, preferably in electric vehicle or automotive industry
  • Strong expertise in 3D modelling, engineering calculations, and product development, with a passion for innovation and sustainability
  • Proficient in NX CAD software and familiar with CAE tools (e.g., ANSYS, Nastran)
  • Experience with casting, forging, and machined parts, including material selection and manufacturing processes, with a focus on lightweight and sustainable materials
  • Strong understanding of vehicle chassis and component design principles, with a focus on electric vehicle architecture and integration
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail and ability to analyze complex problems, leveraging data analytics.
  • Effective communication and collaboration skills, with ability to work with cross-functional teams.
  • Knowledge of drafting standards, including ANSI Y14.5
  • Familiarity with Design for Manufacturability (DFM) and Design for Assembly (DFA) principles
  • Experience with Design Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (DFMEA) and Design Failure Mode and Effects Summary (DFSS)

Nice to Have:

  • Knowledge of Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP) methodology
  • Experience with lean manufacturing principles and six sigma methodologies
  • Proven track record of successfully managing and executing product development projects, with a focus on production rollouts and manufacturing integration
  • Demonstrated experience in collaborating with cross-functional teams, including manufacturing, quality, and testing, to ensure successful product launches
  • Hands-on experience with Wheels and Steering sub-system design and development
